title: Strange fog
description: An unnatural fog clings to the city streets

pitches.title: The Scenic Route
pitches.text: Drivers entering the fog keep emerging outside the same roadside diner, regardless of where they turn. Following an abandoned tram route, the investigators find its ghost driver still making his last run, with the diner now standing on the old terminus. He refuses to finish until someone pays a fare; everyone has been insisting their car should count as a transfer. The investigators buy one ticket and the fog lifts, leaving the diner owner furious that they have fixed his lunch rush.

pitches.title: Exterior Smoke
pitches.text: Fog gathers around a closed theater, and passersby hear an audience coughing inside it. The investigators find a dead stagehand working a supernatural fog machine for a production whose cancellation he refuses to acknowledge. They arrange a final curtain call, which he accepts as proof the show is over. The relieved director immediately describes the haunting as their longest successful run, despite having sold no tickets.

pitches.title: Weatherproof Alibi
pitches.text: Thick fog appears whenever a particular salesman is due home and clears as soon as he arrives. The investigators catch him using a stolen enchanted whistle to summon bad weather, providing a plausible excuse for staying at the bar. They confiscate it, and his wife says she knew the traffic excuse was nonsense because she works across the street. She is chiefly annoyed that he has been ruining her laundry to maintain it.

pitches.title: Please Give Us Some Privacy
pitches.text: A bank of fog crawls along the streets, with wet footprints and stolen fish left in its wake. Tracking the deliveries, the investigators discover two enormous amphibious creatures using the fog as cover while their pond is being dredged. They get the dredging crew to leave one deep pool untouched, and the creatures return home with the fog. Residents who demanded the monsters be removed now complain that their newly unobstructed view is of the dredging crew.

pitches.title: A Very Private Sale
pitches.text: A single block disappears into fog each morning, and people returning from it carry purchases they refuse to discuss. The investigators follow the shoppers to an estate sale, where a cursed privacy screen is concealing the entire property. They fold the screen and expose the supposedly respectable neighbors fighting over the deceased man's enormous collection of erotic ceramics. Everyone agrees the fog was a serious public safety issue once they have finished buying what they came for.

title: Rooftop cryptid
description: A strange form is spotted on rooftops

pitches.title: Restoration Work
pitches.text: A horned creature moves between rooftops at night, leaving broken masonry below. Comparing photographs, the investigators discover that a church gargoyle has come alive and is tearing down newer gargoyles it considers insulting copies of itself. They persuade the restoration contractor to remove the cheap replacements, and it returns to its perch. The contractor bills the church for correcting damage caused by an original feature.

pitches.title: Roof Inspection
pitches.text: Residents report a huge winged shape stalking their homes, shortly before receiving unsolicited roof repair estimates. The investigators stake out the roofing company's warehouse and catch its owner removing a human disguise to reveal a mothlike creature. He really has been inspecting the roofs; the terrifying scratching is his attempt to take measurements without waking anyone. Told that his sales technique is frightening people, he starts making daytime appointments and immediately discovers that everyone was more receptive when they thought the roof might contain a monster.

pitches.title: Up on the Housetop
pitches.text: Something antlered is peering down chimneys, and households find their belongings stacked outside afterward. The investigators trace it to a winter spirit summoned by a shop's badly translated seasonal promotion: instead of bringing gifts, it has been invited to collect them. They correct the invitation and send it away, then help residents retrieve their possessions. Several people insist the spirit can keep presents from their in-laws, who are standing right beside them.

pitches.title: The Good Nesting Schools
pitches.text: An enormous birdlike silhouette is seen carrying patio furniture onto an apartment roof. The investigators follow the stolen furniture to a nest and discover a cryptid preparing to lay an egg. Moving the furniture to an unused water tower persuades it to nest there instead, out of sight. The landlord had already advertised the roof as an exclusive wildlife amenity and objects to losing it before he can raise the rent.

pitches.title: Can You Hear Me Now
pitches.text: A crouching figure with too many limbs keeps appearing beside rooftop antennas, and residents hear muttering through their baby monitors. The investigators locate a stranded alien using the antennas to telephone home, with its private complaints leaking into nearby receivers. They help it make a proper connection and arrange its departure. The supposedly terrifying transmission turns out to be a lengthy argument with its spouse about whether getting stranded counts as an excuse for missing dinner.

title: Strange markings
description: Mysterious graffiti is appearing around town

pitches.title: Wrong Address
pitches.text: The same sinister symbol appears on buildings just before a furious horned visitor pounds on their doors. The investigators find a teenager copying a summoning mark from an occult book because it looks good as a tag. The summoned creature is required to answer every mark and has spent the week being told nobody ordered a demon. Removing the tags releases it, and it demands to know who is going to compensate it for the wasted travel.

pitches.title: Looking for Work
pitches.text: Fresh graffiti appears on walls overnight, offering increasingly desperate messages in an unfamiliar script. The investigators translate it using a book from a local occult collector and learn that an invisible spirit is advertising its services as a guardian. It has been guarding vacant buildings for weeks because it assumes the absence of trouble means customers are satisfied. They refer it to the collector, who wants supernatural protection but immediately asks whether it can also watch his parking space.

pitches.title: The Artist Is Present
pitches.text: Graffiti thought to have been painted over years ago is reappearing, often on buildings that no longer have the same walls. The investigators trace the tags to a dead street artist whose ghost is restoring his work after hearing that it is now valuable. They show him the gallery selling photographs of it for thousands, while the original sites keep getting cleaned. He moves his haunting to the gallery and starts putting his signature across the expensive prints, which the dealer immediately calls a new period.

pitches.title: Crossing Ahead
pitches.text: Unfamiliar marks appear beside storm drains, and cars parked over them acquire deep scratches. Watching a marked drain at night, the investigators find a small underground creature painting warnings for the much larger animal that follows its route. They persuade the town to keep that short stretch of curb clear, allowing both creatures to cross the empty street at night without scraping parked cars. Drivers who complained about the monster promptly complain about the loss of free parking.

pitches.title: The Customer Is Always Here
pitches.text: A restaurant owner reports that threatening writing returns on his wall no matter how often he scrubs it away. The investigators recognize the handwriting of a customer who died after years of complaining about the food and discover his ghost renewing the same bad review. Offering a refund finally makes him leave. The owner refuses until the investigators point out that arguing with a dead customer is costing him more meals than the refund.

pitches.title: Suspiciously Good Boys
pitches.text: Dogs that used to bark at everyone now become silent and obedient whenever one particular dog walker arrives. Following him after work, the investigators discover he is a werewolf whose authority the dogs recognize instantly. He has taken the job because it is the only place his condition earns him compliments. The clients insist the investigators leave him alone, then ask whether his influence might extend to their teenagers.

pitches.title: Still on His Round
pitches.text: Dogs race to their gates and bark at the same time every day, although nobody is visible in the street. The investigators compare the route with an old delivery map and find the ghost of a postal carrier continuing his rounds. Returning his undelivered final letter lets him stop, and the dogs settle down. Its recipient complains that a haunting is an excessive response to being late with a credit card offer.

pitches.title: Off-Leash Training
pitches.text: Dogs across town keep escaping and returning with expensive cuts of meat. The investigators follow one to a locked butcher's shop and catch a young witch practicing animal control instead of paying for groceries. Her own dog keeps ignoring her spells, so she has recruited everyone else's. They confiscate her charm and make her reimburse the butcher; the owners are disappointed to learn their dogs were following commands all along, just never theirs.

pitches.title: Who's a Person
pitches.text: Several residents say their dogs have begun sitting at the dinner table and trying to operate door handles. The investigators trace them to a dog trainer who has been using a cursed collar that temporarily swaps a dog and its owner. He demonstrates obedience by occupying the dog himself, leaving the customer to experience the lesson from the other end of the leash. Once everyone is restored, the trainer's toughest critic admits the praise and treats were more effective than expected and asks about repeat sessions.

pitches.title: Pet Friendly
pitches.text: Dogs on walks refuse to pass one apparently ordinary house, while their owners complain of strange growling from its basement. The investigators discover the tenant keeps a hellhound hidden there and has mistaken its territorial threats for friendly barking. They arrange a discreet move to an isolated property, restoring the dogs' usual route. The tenant is relieved to find somewhere pet friendly after rejecting several perfectly adequate homes because they would not allow a dog large enough to eat the landlord.

title: Erratic electronics
description: Technological devices aren’t behaving like they should

pitches.title: Not Another Upgrade
pitches.text: Phones and computers keep switching themselves off whenever residents discuss buying replacements. The investigators trace the disturbances to a repair shop where a dead technician has been possessing discarded electronics to prove they still work. They get his old apprentice to restore the accumulated machines, giving him a reason to leave. Most of the customers still buy new ones, having now acquired a perfectly reasonable objection to devices that listen to everything they say.

pitches.title: Your Call Is Important
pitches.text: Every telephone in an office begins receiving calls from an employee who died there years ago. The investigators find that her ghost is still at her desk, attempting to complete the customer follow-ups she was promised would earn her a promotion. Her manager admits he invented the target because he never expected anyone to finish it. Told this, she stops calling customers and starts calling him; the employees unanimously report that the problem has been resolved.

pitches.title: It Came with the House
pitches.text: A family's appliances perform household chores in the middle of the night, with increasingly hostile notes appearing on their screens. The investigators discover a house spirit has moved into the smart home system after the family removed its old hearth. It is doing its usual domestic work but objects to being called stupid every time a device misunderstands an instruction. An apology settles the haunting, although the family now has to thank the dishwasher in front of guests.

pitches.title: Free Trial
pitches.text: A neighborhood's devices start playing the same incomprehensible advertisement, even when unplugged. The investigators track the signal to a crashed alien probe that keeps repeating its sales demonstration because nobody has purchased anything. They find the checkout control and place the cheapest possible order, causing it to shut down and depart. The package that follows contains another probe, advertised as an excellent way to introduce friends to the product.

pitches.title: The Previous Owner
pitches.text: A secondhand phone keeps rejecting its new owner's messages and placing calls to an elderly woman instead. The investigators learn its previous owner died while arguing with his mother, and his ghost is using the handset to resume the argument. They connect the call long enough for her to concede the trivial point he has been repeating, allowing him to leave. Once the line is clear, she tells the investigators he was still wrong but she has had enough practice ending conversations with him.
